body.text:
The first thing Nicole did after waking up from the dead was return her boyfriend’s $1,700 birthday gift.

Then she spent every penny she had on food, medicine, weapons, and two steel security doors.

Everyone thought she had gone crazy.

Her boyfriend called her selfish. Her friends laughed at her.

But Nicole knew something they didn’t.

In exactly three days, the city would drown.

And this time, she refused to die for anyone.
——
"Ah!"
Nicole Floyd jolted upright in bed, gasping. Sweat streamed down her forehead, her eyes unfocused and hollow.
The sight in front of her cut through the haze in her mind.
This was her old apartment, the one from before the apocalypse.
Ding, ding…
Text alerts kept chiming. She grabbed her phone from the nightstand.
September 14, 2029. 9:32 a.m.
Nicole had more than a dozen unread messages. All of them were warning about a super typhoon named Cleaver, projected to make landfall early on the 17th along the coast. There would be category-breaking winds and days of relentless rain.
Nicole stared at the screen, dazed.
Hadn't she died? She remembered dying in that cannibal world devoid of light. Had her refusal to accept it dragged her into some dying hallucination?
Ding!
Another alert came in, updated at 9:37 a.m.
Nicole twisted her arm hard. Pain shot up her nerves, sharp and real.
This wasn't a dream. She had been reborn, back to three days before the storm that cracked the world open.
No. To be exact, two and a half days.
Nicole didn't feel happy. The exhaustion had settled deep in her bones. 
Typhoons, floods, deep freeze, extreme heat, earthquakes. One h311 after another. What was there worth reliving?
And yet, she was back.
Was she supposed to sit still and wait to die all over again?
Not a chance!
Nicole splashed cold water on her face. The mirror showed a younger version of herself with smooth skin and clear eyes, no hollowed-out desperation yet.
For a moment, everything looked fine.
Her gaze dropped to the crystal pendant at her neck.
She had been wearing it when she was abandoned at the hospital as a newborn. Later, Edward Austin had taken it from her and given it to the school's beauty queen, Mary Cannon.
Three years into the apocalypse, Mary still looked flawless. Her clothes were clean, her skin rosy, as if the old world never ended for her.
Once, when Nicole collapsed from hunger, she saw Mary casually pull a vanilla ice cream bar out of that pendant and lick it, slow and unbothered.
Nicole's breath hitched.
She grabbed a blade, sliced her fingertip, and let a drop of blood fall onto the pendant.
A blinding light exploded.
When her vision cleared, she stood inside an empty apartment with no front door. There was running water and electricity, but no furniture.
The place had two bedrooms and a living room, totaling about 860 square feet. The ceilings were nearly 10 feet high. Next to the balcony was a small garden, roughly 110 square feet, filled with dark soil.
A glowing timer floated in the living room.
01:56:13.
This was the storage space that let Mary live like royalty. Or rather, the one she had tricked out of Nicole's hands.
When Nicole stepped out, the space stayed with her, embedded in her mind. The moment she focused, she could sense everything inside.
Nicole tested it with boiling water. Everywhere except the balcony and the garden kept things perfectly fresh.
She could store things using thought alone. When nobody entered physically, the timer froze. Once she stepped inside, it started counting down.

Mary stared at the broken pieces, stunned, before letting out a frightened gasp. Seeing his girlfriend upset, Edward exploded and started hurling insults at Nicole.
Nicole's eyes went sharp. "Get lost! And don't ever come back and get in my way!"
Edward's face went gray. He dragged Mary off, furious and humiliated.
Only then did Nicole unlock the stainless steel door and rush inside, tearing open the package.
The polar cold-weather suit was thick but soft, instantly warm when she put it on. The mummy sleeping bag was stitched in layers of down, heavy and solid. These would keep her alive during the deep freeze.
Outside, the wind screamed. The sky had sunk into a deep, heavy black.
Nicole shut all doors and windows tight, pulled out large white plastic barrels, and filled them with water. Several went straight into the storage space bathroom.
Once the typhoon rains fully set in, the complex would lose water and power fast.
No matter how wild it sounded outside, Nicole stayed busy in the kitchen, washing rice, chopping vegetables, cooking nonstop.
Braised beef, roasted chicken with mushrooms, baked fish, and beef and root vegetable stew. Each pot was huge. She packed everything into stainless steel containers, steaming hot, and stored them away.
While the storm had just begun and everyone still had food, it was best to cook strong-smelling dishes now. Later, lighting a fire would only invite trouble.
She steamed dinner rolls, baked bread, and made pastries. The gas stove and induction cooktop ran full blast until well past midnight.
She changed out of her greasy clothes, took a hot shower, and collapsed into bed.
Her sleep was shallow. A drilling noise dragged her awake.
Nicole pulled the curtain aside. Outside was a gray blur, wind and rain howling together. She thought it was still early, but her phone showed it was already after nine in the morning.
WhatsApp was exploding. The neighborhood group and class group both showed over 99 unread messages.
People were cheering the arrival of Typhoon Cleaver. Office workers were celebrating a break from endless overtime. Students were thrilled about the unexpected days off.
Photos and videos flooded the chats: trees ripped out by the roots, luxury cars crushed, a metal factory sliced open by a tornado.
Some people were starting to panic, complaining they hadn't stocked up on food. They said supermarkets were wiped clean by the time they got off work, with only a few sad packs of instant noodles left.
The drilling continued, coming from next door.
Nicole frowned. The building had three units per floor, and the other two were supposed to be empty.
In her last life, floodwater reached the second floor. People who fled their homes never got rescued and started targeting vacant apartments.
At first, everyone kept the peace. As food ran low, eyes grew darker, greed sharper. More than once, they tried to pry open Nicole's door in the middle of the night.
This time, she had a fire axe. If they tried, she wouldn't hesitate.
Then, she heard it. Not just drilling. A child's voice.
Nicole opened her door.
The door to unit 1801 was wide open. A brand-new stainless steel door leaned to the side. A young man in light-colored casual clothes was drilling into the wall.
Hearing her door open, he turned.
Nicole froze.
"It's you?"

body.text:
"Mind Repository. Communication link in progress. All intelligent beings detected and assembled."

Aimee Estrada felt groggy, and her whole body ached as if she had been tightly bound with ropes.

The scorching summer sun burned her skin. Her body instinctively tried to curl up, but she was completely immobilized.

With her waning consciousness, Aimee fought fiercely against her unresponsive body. Finally, her fingers twitched, as if some invisible barrier had shattered.

Regaining control at last, she struggled to open her eyes and pushed herself up with shaking arms.

'Strange. Wasn't I sleeping at home?' Aimee thought, confusion swirling in her mind. Before she could reflect further, a blinding flash of light shot across her vision.

Pain was the last sensation Aimee experienced before slipping back into unconsciousness.

*****

On a vast, endless sea, countless rafts were scattered in every direction, resembling a swarm of black dots on the water. The sight sent chills down one's spine.

"Welcome to Tartasland, players. The sea survival game has officially begun." A cold, mechanical voice echoed across the sea.

At that moment, everyone lying unconscious on their rafts suddenly opened their eyes.

"What is this place?"

"Wh-Who tied me up and put me on this raft?"

"Where am I? I can't swim!"

"Help! Anyone there?"

Similar cries of confusion and panic erupted from rafts across the sea.

Everyone awoke to find themselves in an entirely unfamiliar place, and panic swept through them.

*****

Aimee woke up again, blinking a few times. 'Huh, it doesn't hurt anymore. Was that a weird dream?'

She looked around. Above her was a deep blue sky, and below was clear water. The air was thick with the damp, salty, slightly fishy smell of the sea.

The sun blazed so fiercely that she couldn't look at it directly, and her pajamas were soaked with sweat.

Aimee slowly pushed herself up, focusing on the calm, glassy surface of the sea. The water's clarity felt surreal, yet it was unsettling that nothing could be seen beneath it.

'So it wasn't a dream. Where the hell am I?' Aimee thought again. She rubbed her hands, doubt gnawing at her.

"Dear players, take it easy for now." A lively, human-like mechanical voice, much warmer than the earlier cold announcement, broke through, addressing all players in zone 997.

Suddenly, a flash of blue light appeared in front of Aimee. Then a digital screen showed a cartoonish girl with pigtails and subtitles below her.

"Whoa," Aimee muttered, her brow furrowing.

Then the subtitles made her heart skip a beat.

[I'm System 05 for Zone 997. Welcome to the sea survival game. Please read the rules carefully.]

[1. This is a real place. Please respect every living creature here. If you die here, you die for real.]

[2. All players are between 15 and 50 years old. The elderly and kids stay in your old world, frozen in time. After the rules, you can decide if you want to link your family to your fate.]

[Friendly reminder: Once you bind your family, your life decides theirs.]

[3. Every player starts with a raft (50 square feet) and a novice package.]

[4. The first three days are a Novice Protection Period. It's relatively safe, so gather supplies quickly for the challenges ahead.]

[5. Many treasure chests are scattered across the sea. Open them to get essential supplies.]

[6. Tartasland has many small, uninhabited islands. Each is a mix of opportunity and danger. Be careful when exploring.]

[Alright, everyone, the ultimate survival game is now live. Best of luck to you all.]

The screen disappeared instantly, and a stream of silvery light swirled around Aimee's wrist. A metallic watch shimmered into view, showing the time, 7:50 AM.

Aimee was only 23, fresh out of college, and she was an avid webnovel fan. She had a hunch about what was happening. She twisted her wrist, checked the watch, and tapped the round center button.

The blue screen appeared again, resembling a phone app, with tabs for Profile, Mailbox, Trade Hall, Chat Channel, System Bag, and more.

Suddenly, the system addressed Aimee directly. The subtitles matched what she heard in her ear.

[Dear Player 658234166, would you like to generate a new name?]

[Do you want to change your player name? If you don't answer before the timer runs out, the system will default to your current one.]

'Who uses their real name online?' Aimee thought, quickly tapping "Yes" and changing her nickname to Lucky.

Lucky was the dog Aimee had as a kid. Since Lucky's passing, she'd consistently used that name and avatar online.

When Aimee checked her profile, it had changed to:

[Name: Lucky]

[Age: 23]

[Health: 100/100]

[Energy: 60/100 (Hot and exhausted. In need of water and food.)]

[Strength: 4/10 (Human max is 10. Average is 6. Below human average strength.)]

[Agility: 3/10 (Below human average.)]

[Mentality: 100/100 (?!)]

[Talent: Not unlocked]

[Skill: Not unlocked]

Aimee stared at her profile, sensing something odd.

[Mentality: 100/100 (?!)]

Aimee didn't know what mentality was or how to use it, but the system's apparent shock indicated its importance.

Suddenly, a box resembling a game loot package appeared before her.

[Novice package delivered. Would you like to open it?]

Aimee rubbed her eyes in disbelief. As she grappled with the bizarre situation, the item's sudden appearance shattered any remaining hope. She pushed aside her swirling thoughts and said, "Yes."

[Novice package opened successfully. Congratulations! You've received: Dry Bread x1, Novice Fishing Rod x1, Talent Awakening Stone x1.]

The novice package contained only three items. The first two were obvious from their names.

However, Aimee's mind kept circling back to the last one. 'Talent Awakening Stone?'

[Talent Awakening Stone detected. This item is the only way for humans to unlock special powers. Use it to unlock a random talent. No levels. It's all up to luck.]

[Do you want to use the Talent Awakening Stone to unlock a talent randomly?]

Aimee glanced down at the shabby raft beneath her. It seemed ready to flip with one wave. Then she remembered the dry bread and the fishing rod from the package.

Without hesitation, she chose to use it. 'No point in hesitating. Might as well take a gamble. I've been pretty lucky already.'

The screen erupted in a burst of rainbow light, exploding with color.

Aimee's heart raced. 'With colors like that, this must be a super lucky draw! I've always had the worst luck in gacha games and never won the lottery. Is this finally my lucky break?'

She focused on the package, fists clenched in nervous anticipation. But then, the rainbow glow gradually faded, transforming into a dull white light. Her chest tightened. 'Come on, seriously? Am I this unlucky?' she thought.

..............................................................................
[Congratulations, Lucky, on acquiring the talent: Omniscient Eyes (Basic).]

"Talent detected! Talent Ranking is now live."

Meanwhile, a notification from System 05 appeared before Aimee.

[Congratulations on being the first player to unlock the Talent Ranking. Reward: Bronze Chest x1. Do you wish to hide your information? If no choice is made within 10 seconds, the system will automatically select Yes.]

"No!" Aimee exclaimed, her face turning pale. 'Standing out makes you a target,' she thought. Though she awakened a talent, she was still a complete newbie with nothing to show for it.

[Congratulations to the player from Zone XXX for being the first to unlock a talent. Reward: Bronze Chest x1.]

A new ranking list suddenly appeared on the right side of the screen.

Aimee tapped it, confirming it was the Talent Ranking.

[Talent Ranking: First Place: XXX; Talent: XXX, Zone: XXX]

For now, she was the only player in the survival game to have unlocked a talent.

'Thank goodness I acted quickly,' Aimee thought, breathing a sigh of relief. 'If I hadn't, I'd be in trouble. I'm still a total novice, barely able to do anything. Guess I got lucky with this talent.'

Meanwhile, the Chat Channel below was flooded with over 999 messages. The chat was buzzing.

[Holy crap. Did you guys hear that? Talent! This game actually has talents.]

[Who is this person? Stop hiding. We're all Blunitolings here. We should stick together and get through this mess!]

[Bronze Chest? Why is the gap between players so huge?]

[I skipped meals for my diet, and now I'm literally starving. Can anyone help me out with some food? Once I get some supplies, I'll pay you back.]

[Hey, big shot, show yourself and tell us how to awaken a talent.]

[Guys, this is the server Chat Channel. That pro might not be here. Stop badgering.]

[More people made it onto the ranking. Seriously, how do you awaken a talent?]

'Wait, someone else made it onto the ranking?' Aimee thought, quickly going back to the Talent Ranking. Sure enough, three more names had appeared. 'Looks like there are plenty of Talent Awakening Stones. A few more people have popped up in a few minutes.'

Those who came second and third also chose to keep their information private. The ranking was slowly adding new names, which indicated an abundance of Talent Awakening Stones.

'I guess it all comes down to luck for your talent,' Aimee thought as she returned to her profile.

The talent section was now accessible.

[Talent: Omniscient Eyes (Basic)]

[Detection Range: 30 feet]

[Core Ability: Identify the exact location of all items within 30 feet and provide a written description. Higher ability levels yield more detailed descriptions. Detect rare items within 600 feet.]

[Additional Feature: At the basic level, one can see through obstacles like wood and glass. Rarity of items is color-coded.]

[Limitation: Each use costs 10 Mentality Points. Exceeding 3 minutes causes temporary blurry vision.]

[Note: This is the only talent in all zones that gains new abilities with each level up. To progress to the next stage, you'll need XXX, XXX, and XXX.]

Aimee's hands trembled as she read the talent description. She was so thrilled that she could hardly breathe. 'What is this? This is not only a talent but also a cheat code. Is this the plot twist my dull luck has been craving?' she thought.

She couldn't stop smiling. The fear of being thrust into this strange game was fading away.

"I can't celebrate too soon," Aimee muttered, exhaling deeply. "Supplies are crucial now, and I still don't know what I need for the next upgrade." For now, she only had one piece of Dry Bread. Getting food and water was her top priority.

[Please review the Novice Protection Period rules.]

A new message appeared on Aimee's watch. She straightened up, her expression turning serious. In games like this, the Novice Protection Period was the prime time to gather supplies. It allowed players a few days to acclimate.

[Novice Protection Period Rules:]

[1. For the first three days, beast spawn rates are 20% on day one. Then it'll increase by 30% each subsequent day. Adapt quickly, folks.]

[2. Your raft's durability won't decrease during the Novice Protection Period. Upgrade your raft while you can.]

[3. Chest drops are doubled during this period. You can fish for chests for basic supplies.]

[4. Beast attacks are reduced by 60% during the protection period. Common beasts won't disturb your raft unless you enter the water or seek them out.]

[5. Nights are dangerous. Guard your raft. Unless you're significantly overpowered, avoid searching for supplies after dark.]

After reviewing the rules, Aimee tried to understand the situation. Essentially, during the Novice Protection Period, there'd be fewer beasts. Their attacks would be weaker, and more double chests would be available.

Yet, despite the seemingly positive news, a sense of dread loomed. 'I've only got three days to gather supplies, upgrade my raft, and get stronger,' Aimee thought.

Her raft measured only 50 square feet. It was so cramped that turning around was a challenge. She awkwardly took the fishing rod from the novice package.

This was her main opportunity for supplies, but she had no clue how to fish. 'Do I only need to cast the line and wait?' she wondered.

Not far away, a wooden box suddenly appeared, bobbing on the waves.

Aimee's eyes brightened. She swiftly cast her fishing rod at the box, and miraculously, the hook snagged it.

She reeled the box to her raft's edge and carefully pulled it up. The light brown box felt surprisingly weightless in her hands.

[You've obtained 1 Wooden Chest. Do you want to open it?]

"Yes!" Aimee exclaimed, staring at the chest as if praying. 'Please let there be water,' she thought.

[Congratulations! You've received: Pasta x2, 10 fl oz Mineral Water x1, and Lumber x2.]

Aimee was ecstatic. She'd been drifting for ages without a drop of water.

Chests changed the game for her. She decided to use her Omniscient Eyes, spending 10 Mentality Points to activate them.

Suddenly, everything snapped into focus. She could see even the smallest ripples in the water. White spots appeared around her raft, and one green spot stood out.

She quickly memorized the locations of a few white spots, and before she knew it, her minute was up.

Aimee paddled her raft over to the three white spots she'd spotted, and sure enough, three Wooden Chests floated there.

'The white spots must mark Wooden Chests,' she thought. 'If the color glow indicates rarity, then green must signal higher-level loot. But that green spot is too far. Might as well retrieve the nearby white spots first.'

She eagerly opened the three Wooden Chests she had pulled in.

[You've obtained: Canned Pasta x1, Lumber x4, 3.3 fl oz Mineral Water x2, Iron Piece x2, and 3.5oz Compressed Biscuits x1.]

That was all Aimee got from three chests. 'Maybe others are finding better loot?' she wondered.

Aimee checked the time. It was already 11:30. Her Energy Point was down to 30, and she felt lightheaded. She quickly maneuvered her raft next to a chest, grabbed her dry bread and mineral water, and dug in.

She kept busy by glancing at the Chat Channel. The message count was over 999 again. 'Even with everyone scrambling to survive, people still loved to chat,' she thought.

[Why is there so little in these chests? One bottle of water? Are they expecting us to survive on that?]

[Really? I think it's not that bad. Open a few more chests, and you'll find water and bread. Survival is easy if you try. Maybe you haven't opened enough yet.]

[I still don't know how to unlock a talent. We all started at the same place, and now they're suddenly ahead. Why are they progressing while I'm still stuck?]

..............................................................................
The chat buzzed about loot from the chests until someone mentioned talents, and the channel fell silent.

"I also want to know how to unlock one. I'm already useless, and without a talent, isn't this suicide at sea?"

"Seriously, does no one know how?"

"Whatever, since no one's sharing, I'm here to see if anyone's got extra food. Hit me up in Trade Hall."

"Bread for Mineral Water, anyone?"

The topic quickly shifted.

Aimee munched on her bread, watching the chat scroll by, completely unfazed.

'Anyone foolish enough to stick their neck out now is asking for trouble,' she thought. No way was she taking that risk. She packed her belongings and tossed everything into her System Bag. Her supplies were meager. She needed more chests.

Later, she found four more wooden chests.

[You've received: Wind-Proof Lighter x1, Lumber x6, 3.5oz Compressed Biscuits x1, 7 fl oz Cola x1, and Iron Piece x4.]

'Not bad,' Aimee thought. 'The system even offered Cola.' She gazed at the familiar logo in her hand. It felt like ages since she'd last seen one. She almost cried but couldn't shed a tear, missing her old, monotonous routine.

She took a sip of the Cola and got back to work. Time was of the essence. She paddled with her hands, activated her Omniscient Eyes, and continued towards the next chest.

Three hours later, she'd opened seven more chests:

[You've gained: Brioche x3, Canned Beef Stew x1, Plastic x3, Twine Rope x2, Fever Reducer x1, Lumber x36, Iron Piece x20, 10 fl oz Mineral Water x4, Old Fishing Net x1, 33.8 fl oz Mineral Water x1, and 7oz Sandwich Biscuits x1.]

[You've met the requirements to upgrade your raft to level one. Do you want to upgrade now?]

"So I can upgrade now?" Aimee asked, glancing at the screen in confusion. The raft icon glowed in the top right corner.

[Level-1 Raft Upgrade Materials: Lumber x48/10, Iron Piece x26/10, Twine Rope x2/1, Plastic x3/2.]

Twine Ropes and Plastic were also needed for the upgrade, and Aimee had acquired them from the chests. She couldn't hide her excitement, rubbing her fingers together.

'It's all about collecting as much as possible. The more chests I open, the better the loot,' she thought. "Upgrade!"

The moment her raft was upgraded, it transformed. The original 50 square feet expanded to 100 square feet, giving her enough room to turn around. She was thrilled.

Two paddles appeared on either side of the raft. She tentatively stomped on the floor and felt the difference. It was much sturdier now. There was no need to tiptoe anymore.

The raft section on her screen updated again.

[Level-1 Raft to Level-2 Raft]

[Basic Materials: Lumber x200, Iron Piece x80, Plastic x50]

[Advanced Materials: Twine Rope x20, Resin x10, Beast Bone x1]

Seeing the requirements had skyrocketed, Aimee felt overwhelmed. She hadn't even encountered Resin or Beast Bone yet.

Just then, the familiar System Broadcast rang out again. "Congrats, Lucky! You're the first to upgrade your raft. Want to announce it? If you share it with players in all zones, you'll earn a Silver Chest as a reward."

'So the rules are changing,' Aimee thought. 'The system is pushing players into different ranks now. If I go public, I get a Silver Chest.

'Raft upgrades are nothing like talents. Someone would have leveled up soon anyway. I only got a head start on the basic loot because of my talent.'

"Notification!" Everyone hustling for chests suddenly heard the System Broadcast.

"Congrats to Lucky from Zone 997 for being the first to upgrade their raft successfully and earn a Silver Chest. Keep up the good work, everyone!"

"Raft Level Ranking is now live!"

[Man, we're still grinding for chests while someone upgraded their raft quietly!]

[Shit. That's so unfair!]

[Zone 997? That's us. Hey, Lucky, show yourself and chat with us!]

[Wow, Silver Chest? I'm still scavenging for lumber, and they already got one Silver Chest. That's brutal.]

[Yeah, Lucky, speak up.]

[Lucky, share your survival tips. You've upgraded. Give us some pointers.]

"Congrats to Player Flatline from Zone 666 for upgrading their raft, earning Bronze Chest x3."

"Congrats to Player Mondris from Zone 8760 on earning Bronze Chest x2."

System Broadcasts rang out, shifting the focus away from Aimee.

The Raft Level Ranking lit up right after.

Since Aimee was the first to upgrade, she held the top spot even though others caught up at the same level.

Aimee checked her profile again. Her mentality was at 71 out of 100.

She'd used Omniscient Eyes three times. Each use drained 10 points. That extra 1 point must have regenerated on its own.

Suddenly, Aimee had a bold idea. 'What if I use Omniscient Eyes on my own profile? What will happen?' Feeling a chill, she decided to try it anyway. The text on her screen then shifted.

[Profile:]

[Player Name: Lucky (Name changed)]

[Age: 23]

[Health: 1,000/1,000. Health decreases when injured. It can be restored with a recovering potion. If health drops below 30, recovery becomes impossible.]

[Energy: 46/200. Energy decreases when fatigued. It regenerates automatically, recovering 1 point per minute. If energy drops below 20, your body feels powerless.]

[Strength: 4/10]

[Agility: 3/10]

[Mentality: 71/200]

[Talent: Omniscient Eyes (Basic)

[Detection Range: 30 feet

[Core Ability: Instantly spot every item within 30 feet and get a detailed description. The higher your talent level, the more info you receive. Rarity shows as different colors. More features unlock as you explore.

[Additional Feature: At the basic level, you can see through items like lumber and glass. Higher levels allow you to see through tougher materials.

[Limitations: Costs 10 mentality points per use. If it lasts over 3 minutes, your vision gets fuzzy.

[Requirements for Level-1 Upgrade:

[1. Probe over 100 items in total.

[2. Probe an area greater than 500 square feet.

[3. Lunar Radiance Essence x3. Obtainable by using your talent to condense night sea mist or defeating a Level-3 Beast, the Lunar Jellyfish. Various ways to obtain.

[4. Glimmer Crystal x10. Commonly found inferior energy ores.

[5. On the Lunar Radiance Night, expose the items to enhance your Omniscient Eyes.]

Aimee was shocked by the upgrade requirements for Omniscient Eyes, almost biting her tongue. "If I hadn't checked my talent with Omniscient Eyes, I probably wouldn't have known how to level up, even after a hundred years."

She shook her head in frustration, her mouth twisting into a bitter smile. She noticed her Health Point increased after upgrading her Talent. 'Is that how it works? Will leveling up my talent boost my health points?' she wondered.

The next upgrade required defeating a Level-3 Beast, which felt far out of her reach. She didn't even have a weapon.

But it was a wake-up call for Aimee. Her talent focused on support, not survival. If real trouble hit, she'd be defenseless. Relying on chests was a gamble. 'I should check out the Trade Hall instead,' she thought.

..............................................................................
For now, Aimee had plenty of food and water. She turned the raft with her paddle and let it drift toward the green chest. Then, she opened the Trade Hall on her screen.

MoonlitHeart: [Trading 1 bag of bread for 1 bottle of mineral water.]

Gunrunner: [Offering plastic for any food.]

Aimee scrolled through the Trade Hall, but most were looking to swap for food, not weapons.

'That makes sense, thought. Everyone is starting fresh, scrambling for basics,' she thought, and then opened the Chat Channel, which was buzzing with activity.

Sweetie: [Any cute guys want to DM me? One piece of bread, and I'm all yours.]

[God, weren't the chests supposed to be doubled? I've searched forever and only found 3. Water? I'm dying of thirst here.]

[Meet me in the Trade Hall. Trading food for water.]

[Plastic for water.]

[It's so hot, and I'm exhausted. How can I fish for chests like this?]

Clearly, everyone was short of food and water now.

Aimee posted quickly: [I got food and water, looking to trade for weapons. DM me if interested.]

It was cool that one could send pics in chat, so Aimee sent photos of her brioche and 3.3 fl oz Mineral Water.

The chat exploded when Aimee, who came first on the Raft Level Ranking, appeared.

[Selfie with the pro, please!]

[Lucky, how do you level up your raft?]

[Pro, can you help with my raft?]

[Come on. Share the secret. How do we level up our rafts?]

Messages kept flooding in, and her DMs were about to blow up.

Luckily, Aimee had turned off friend requests. She opened her DMs, ready to sort through the chaos.

[Hey, can we trade for something else? I've got lumber.]

Aimee thought, 'I've got enough lumber. No thanks.'

[Pro, you're amazing! Can I join you?]

[Hey, cutie. One piece of bread, and I'll chat with you. You can do anything you want.]

Aimee thought, 'What's this rubbish? Bah.'

Gunrunner: [Trading 1 dagger for 1 Brioche and 1 bottle of Mineral Water.]

Meanwhile, far south of Aimee, a tall, tanned woman on a raft piled high with plastic frowned at her screen, waiting for a reply that never came.

"Did I ask for too much?" she muttered. She looked helplessly at her raft overflowing with plastic. "Maybe I should offer plastic instead. Anyone trading for weapons this early must know how valuable plastic is, right?"

She had just realized that plastic was a key material for upgrading the raft. Suddenly, all that plastic she had found so annoying didn't seem so bad anymore.

Meanwhile, Aimee wasn't concerned about the offer. She was focused on fishing for chests.

Earlier, she had maneuvered her raft to get closer to the green chest, but unexpectedly, the raft drifted right beside the chest.

Aimee grabbed her fishing rod, gave it a flick, and snagged the chest onto her raft. It was a Bronze Chest.

From what she'd seen, a white glow indicated a Wooden Chest, while a green glow pointed to a Bronze Chest.

Aimee smiled as she hoisted the Bronze Chest onto her raft, feeling a surge of excitement.

[Congratulations! You've obtained a Bronze Chest.]

Aimee now possessed 2 Bronze Chests and one Silver Chest.

She hadn't opened the chests from the reward of the Talent Ranking and Raft Level Ranking yet, but there was no hurry.

Her DMs were filling up with notifications. She quickly filtered out unwanted messages, especially from leeches seeking freebies. Then she quickly focused on a player, Gunrunner.

Lucky: [Deal. Let's do it in the Trade Hall.]

There were two trading methods: privately, off the books to avoid fees, or through the Trade Hall, the official channel that charged a commission. However, during the Novice Protection Period, the Trade Hall waived all fees.

Gunrunner: [Deal.]

Seeing Aimee finally respond, Gunrunner felt relieved. Noticing she still hadn't obtained any food, she sent another message. [Wanna trade plastic for your mineral water. Is it okay?]

Aimee got a normal dagger from Gunrunner after placing the brioche and mineral water in the trade slot. Before she could examine it, another message arrived.

'Plastic for Mineral Water? Sure, why not?' Aimee thought, checking her stash: 3.3 fl oz Mineral Water x1, 10 fl oz Mineral Water x5, and 33.8 fl oz Mineral Water x1.

Lucky: [How much plastic do you have? What kind of deal are you looking for?]

Gunrunner quickly swallowed her bread when she saw Lucky's reply. However, she almost choked on her food. 'This bread is so dry. I need water now,' she thought.

Gunrunner: [Plastic x2 for 3.3 fl oz Mineral Water x1]

Aimee thought the offer was not so ideal. While plastic was essential for raft upgrades, most players were struggling for supplies. Water was more important than plastic.

Lucky: [That's overpriced. Right now, water's worth more than basic materials. I'll trade 3.3 fl oz Mineral Water for 3 pieces of Plastic. I have two bottles of 10 fl oz Mineral Water. 18 pieces of Plastic for both. If you're not interested, forget it.]

'10 fl oz Mineral Water? Deal,' Gunrunner thought, grinning. 'It's a bit steep, but two 10 fl oz bottles should last me at least a day.'

Gunrunner: [Do you have more food? I can trade plastic for more.]

Aimee raised an eyebrow. 'Gunrunner seems to be a plastic tycoon. Despite all the chests I've fished up, I still don't have as much plastic as Gunrunner does.

'Trading plastic for food? Did Gunrunner only get plastic from chests? I can't let this deal slip. Plastic will be crucial for upgrades.'

Lucky: [Yes, I do. Plastic x2 for Brioche x1, Plastic x2 for Pasta x1, Plastic x5 for Canned Pasta x1, and Plastic x10 for 3.5oz Compressed Biscuit x1.]

Seeing Aimee's message, Gunrunner, who had been lounging with her legs crossed, shot up abruptly.

'Man, pros really live differently,' she thought. 'I'm still on Dry Bread, and she's already got Canned Pasta. I've been eating stale bread for a whole day.'

Gunrunner: [I'll take the Canned Pasta, Compressed Biscuit, and Pasta.]

Aimee: [Deal. That's 45 Plastic total. Let's do this in the Trade Hall.]

The plastic arrived swiftly. Now Aimee had 46 plastic. She was nearly ready for her next upgrade. 'Gunrunner truly is a plastic tycoon,' Aimee thought as she sent a friend request.

Lucky: [Let's add each other. If we have extras later, we can trade again.]

Gunrunner accepted instantly.

*****

As time went by, Aimee opened four more Wooden Chests.

By 7 PM, the sky began to darken. Remembering the system's reminder, Aimee promptly abandoned the remaining chests.

Despite recovering, her energy was only at 46/100. She sank onto her raft, feeling utterly exhausted. She still had two Bronze Chests and one Silver Chest unopened.

Trusting her instincts, Aimee felt uneasy in the night, as if something was lurking nearby. With her stash feeling less secure, she opted to open the Bronze Chests first.

[Congratulations! You've obtained: Workbench Blueprint (Basic) x1, Wooden Gazebo Blueprint (Basic) x1, Candle x2, Winter Windbreaker x1, Seasons Pajama x4, Whale Oil Lamp x1, Hemostatic Potion x2, Energy Recovering Potion x2, Iron Piece x15, Lumber x40, Plastic x20, Fabric x5, Twine Rope x10, Resin x5.]

Opening the Bronze Chests was an entirely new experience. She received supplies she'd never seen before in impressive quantities. The Workbench Blueprint caught her attention the most.

..............................................................................
[Workbench Blueprint (Basic): Repair your weapons and gear, or craft various items with the right blueprints. Required materials: Lumber x30, Plastic x15, Iron Piece x6, Twine Rope x2.]

[Wooden Gazebo Blueprint (Basic): A simple gazebo, ideal for shielding from sun and rain. Required materials: Lumber x45, Iron Piece x5, Twine Rope x1. Place them on the workbench to make one.]

To build the Wooden Gazebo, Aimee needed a workbench first. It seemed the workbench was essential. She checked her system bag.

Building it would leave her with few basic materials, but she needed that workbench. 'Forget it. Let me see what's in the Silver Chest first,' she thought. 'The Bronze Chest gave me so much. The Silver Chest must be even better.'

[Congratulations! You've opened the Silver Chest and received: Silvermoon Bow (Level 2) x1, Simple Encyclopedia x1, Glimmer Crystal x2, Antidote Potion x3, Warm Clothing Design x1, Health Recovering Potion x2, Lumber x120, Plastic x70, Iron Piece x50, Twine Rope x30, Resin x20.]

Aimee was overwhelmed with excitement. One Silver Chest felt like getting two or three Bronze Chests. The highlights were two blueprints and a weapon.

She picked up the Silvermoon Bow, which shimmered with iridescent colors, leaving her uncertain about what metal it was made from. It was strikingly beautiful and practical. She tested the string. It was smooth and effortless.

[Silvermoon Bow (Level 2): A Level-2 weapon crafted by the Elvenfolk, designed for young elves in the hunt. Durability: 200/200.]

'Elvenfolk? So there are other sentient races in this continent,' Aimee thought, her heartbeat quickening. 'If it were only humans, survival would be an internal struggle. But with other intelligent races, it's a fight for all.'

She rubbed her fingertips uneasily. 'Never mind. There's no point in thinking about this now. The most important thing is to focus on what's right in front of me,' she thought, shaking her head.

It was already 8 PM, and the sea breeze was picking up, swirling around her.

Aimee shivered and quickly pulled out her winter pajamas from the system bag, changing into them before grabbing her windbreaker for additional warmth.

*****

The next morning at 8 AM, Aimee was awakened by the system's voice.

"Good morning, players. A new day has arrived. Let's start another survival round. Beasts have a 50% chance of appearing today. Good luck!"

Aimee skipped washing up, grabbed some bread, took a sip of water, and started organizing her supplies. She planned to construct the workbench first and then check if she could upgrade her raft to level 2.

Her raft still felt cramped. Once the workbench was set up, there would likely be no space left.

[Do you want to spend Lumber x30, Plastic x10, Iron Piece x6, and Twine Rope x2 to build the workbench?]

"Yes," Aimee replied.

[Congratulations, Lucky! You've successfully built the workbench.]

[Workbench: It unlocks crafting of simple items without blueprints and crafting with blueprints.]

'That's it? What brevity,' Aimee thought. She placed the workbench at the very top of her raft, ensuring it occupied more than 30 square feet.

The raft remained too cramped. With the workbench consuming so much space, Aimee struggled to turn over at night without bumping her head. She'd have to change that habit. Falling off would be disastrous.

Her eagerness to upgrade her raft increased. It was too small, and she still had no idea where to find Beast Bones. She thought maybe she needed to hunt some beasts for them.

She felt puzzled. 'It's only the second day of the Novice Protection Period, and the chance of beasts appearing is supposed to be higher. I should have encountered at least one by now.' Curious, she opened the Chat Channel to see what others were experiencing.

The chat was already buzzing.

[Damn, anyone got any Healing Potion? I'll trade my supplies for some!]

[Help! There are so many beasts circling my raft.]

[Food for Healing Potion!]

[Does anyone have water? Please, I'm dying of thirst!]

[What the hell is this place? I want to go home!]

[Help! The beasts broke through the shield.]

One of the avatars that had been talking instantly turned gray.

Compared to yesterday's lively chatter, the Chat Channel was now in chaos.

The player count in Zone 997 had already fallen to 98,952 out of 100,000. In one day, over a thousand had vanished.

Yesterday, most players doubted the system's warnings about death. Today, however, they witnessed it firsthand. One moment, they were chatting, and the next, someone's avatar turned gray. Yet, not everyone panicked. A few players remained calm.

Snacktime: [Guys, remember the novice protection rules. If you actually read them, you can avoid a lot of trouble.]

[Exactly! If people bothered to read the novice rules, they wouldn't face any issues. However, some don't care if they live or die.]

[It's easy for you to mock. They might not mean to provoke the beasts.]

[But didn't the novice protection rules say common beasts can't attack the raft by themselves?]

That message quickly got lost in a flood of comments. There was no telling how many people saw it.

Many encountered beasts, so something was off on Aimee's end. As she watched the numbers drop on the screen, she fell silent.

All her accomplishments stemmed from luck, but she didn't know how long it would last. To secure her place in this ocean, she had to level up and grow stronger, without wasting her talent, Omniscient Eyes.

She activated her Omniscient Eyes and paddled toward the treasure chests. To the left, three Wooden Chests beckoned, and to the right, two more.

Aimee continued paddling for treasure until 11 PM when her energy hit 30 and fell into the red zone. She quickly lay down to rest.

Waving her hand to cool off, she noticed the wild temperature swings. Night and day felt completely different. After a bit, she was drenched in sweat, so she changed into her summer pajamas.

[Congratulations to Player Gunrunner in Zone 997 for defeating a beast above their level. Reward: Silver Chest x1.]

'Someone already took down a beast above their level?' Aimee thought, stunned, her eyes wide. She hadn't even encountered a beast yet, and someone else had slain one above their level.

Players in Zone 997 were going wild.

[Whoa, another pro. Zone 997 really is the chosen one!]

[So jealous. I'm still here, grabbing chests and dodging beasts while someone's already killed one above their level!]

Gunslinger: [Not bad! I took out a common beast, expected a reward, but got nothing. So all that effort was pointless unless you take on a beast stronger than you, huh?]

[Respect! You're awesome, too. Wanna team up? I've got cool stuff to trade.]

[All hail to you, Gunslinger!] x10

"Already sucking up? So lame," Aimee muttered, lurking in the chat while eating. She sighed, thinking, 'No way I can compete with that.'

Gunrunner suddenly messaged her: [Beast Bone for Healing Potion. Got any?]

'Healing Potion?' Aimee's eyes widened. She quickly replied: [Are you hurt?]

Gunrunner, weakly sprawled on her raft, pressed a hand to her wounded abdomen. [Yeah, I am. Do you have any Healing Potions? If not, I'll ask someone else.]

Aimee searched her supplies, muttering inwardly, 'How could a Silver Chest not have a Healing Potion? That's stingy!' Then she immediately agreed to offer help.

Lucky: [Hemostatic Potion for Beast Bone, and throw in some info about the beasts, too.]

Gunrunner: [Deal.]

Salma Warren, Gunrunner, grabbed the Hemostatic Potion and drank it. The bleeding stopped almost instantly. She discreetly tied a corner of her shirt around her waist.

"Good thing it didn't hit anything vital." Gunrunner gritted her teeth, pulling the makeshift bandage tight.

'Being friends with a top player has its perks. They have plenty of resources,' she thought. 'I must have sent dozens of messages in the Chat Channel and heard nothing back, or people tried to exploit me once they knew I was injured.'

She shifted into a more comfortable position and lay back, realizing she wouldn't be fishing for treasure chests today. But it didn't matter. Deast drops were far better than anything from a chest. Whenever she opened one, it was always plastic anyway.

..............................................................................
Salma shared details about the creature she encountered with Lucky.

Gunrunner: [I spotted a crab-like beast with three eyes, definitely mutated. Its claws are razor-sharp. One hit took 20 points off my novice shield's durability.]

Gunrunner: [The system informed me I discovered a new rule for the novice phase: if you face a Level-2 Beast, its attack is weakened by 80%.]

Gunrunner: [I later noticed its belly, despite being mutated, was unarmored. It's the weak spot. After defeating it, the system identified it as a Timbercrab, a Level-2 Beast. It dropped a Silver Chest and some other loot.]

Gunrunner: [If you're unsure about facing it, don't try. If you see one, run.]

Aimee placed the gauze she received from the chest into the gift section of her friend list.

Lucky: [A thank-you gift.]

Gunrunner: [No need. Your Hemostatic Potion was effective. You earned the info.]

Lucky: [We'll likely trade again. Let's support each other and be friends.]

Aimee insisted on sending the gauze. Gifts were one-way, no returns anyway.

Salma noticed the gauze Aimee sent. It was far better than her sweat-soaked fabric, so she didn't think twice.

Gunrunner: [Alright, thanks. Next time I trade, you'll be my first choice.]

Aimee sent an OK gesture. This system was impressive. It could send pictures and emojis, like a smartphone.

Although she traded a Hemostatic Potion for the info, how much one would share was up to them. Gunrunner shared so much with her. It was right for her to return the favor with a piece of gauze.

While reading the messages, Aimee didn't waste time. She opened four chests.

[Lumber x20, Iron Piece x10, Plastic x5, Resin x3, 10 fl oz Mineral Water x1, Strawberry Cream Bread x2, Pasta x1, Gauze x3]

She felt her supplies had increased again today. Four Wooden Chests yielded considerable loot, and to her surprise, there was pasta.

Aimee had been craving real food for days and was practically drooling at the thought.

She quickly pulled out the pasta, which was still steaming hot. She couldn't wait to eat, shoveling a few bites into her mouth. "That's the flavor I've missed!"

After finishing her meal, she realized she had no place for the plate and fork. Tossing them overboard wasn't an option. Littering the ocean was unacceptable.

The chests she found were from the sea, so she decided to toss the used items into an empty chest for now and focus on gathering more intel.

She activated her Omniscient Eyes and spotted a bright red glow. Compared to the scattered white dots, the red one stood out sharply. She quickly steered her raft in that direction.

She didn't let any Wooden Chests pass by, either. Uncertain about the red glow and seeing it was quite far off, she prioritized the white loot spots.

While collecting chests, Aimee couldn't shake one thought. 'Gunrunner mentioned their novice shield's durability had been chipped away, huh?'

She checked the newbie guide again, and it read: [During the protection period, all beasts have their attack reduced by 60%, and common beasts won't attack the raft.]

'It only mentioned common beasts not attacking the raft, indicating that "common" referred to one level, and there were others, like Level-2 Beasts,' Aimee thought. Once she realized this, she felt frustrated. 'What a scam.'

She opened the Fighting Force Ranking on her screen. Players from all races were listed. Gunrunner was at the top, having already taken down a Level-2 Beast, while others had only managed common beasts.

Aimee, at the absolute bottom, wasn't even on the list, and she felt helpless.

Suddenly, a small wave hit, rocking Aimee's raft, but everything on board remained intact. As she activated her Omniscient Eyes, little halos of light appeared before her.

"Wow, this area hasn't been explored yet. The chests are overflowing," Aimee exclaimed, pulling out an old fishing net from her System Bag. It was worn down, with only 50 durability left, but perfect for the moment.

Fishing for chests one by one was tedious. She darted around, scooping up chests as quickly as possible.

Then an explosion rocked the raft, nearly flipping it over.

Aimee pressed against the deck, scrambling to maintain balance.

In the distance, an eerie hum rolled over the sea, haunting and deep, like thunder resonating with sadness, making the ocean tremble.

Waves crashed toward Aimee, one after another, as the raft's alarm blared like a warning siren.

[Raft under attack. Novice shield activated. Shield durability reduced by 70.]

[Raft under attack. Shield durability reduced by 10.]

[Shield durability reduced to 0. Novice shield has disappeared.]

[Raft affected. Raft sturdiness reduced by 1.]

The alerts continued blaring while the waves tossed the raft around.

Aimee's heart raced, almost leaping out of her chest. 'What the hell is happening? The raft's durability plummeted to 0. If this continues, the raft will be lost. Is there a way to boost its sturdiness? Wait, upgrading! Leveling up the raft increases sturdiness.'

"System, upgrade the raft," she commanded.

[Consuming Lumber x200/355, Iron Piece x80/106, Plastic x50/98, Twine Rope x20/54, Resin x10/21, Timbercrab Beast Bone x1/1. Raft being upgraded...]

A flash of light enveloped Aimee, and finally, the raft's alarm silenced.

The raft, once 100 square feet, had now expanded to 300 square feet, like the floor of a small room. The workbench remained in place.

[Congratulations, Lucky! You're the first to upgrade your raft to Level 2. Do you want to broadcast this to all zones? If you do, you'll earn a Silver Chest.]

"Y-Yes," she replied, letting out a sigh of relief as the raft finally steadied. Her ears still buzzed from the explosion. She hadn't expected the announcement to blare directly in her mind.

After upgrading the raft, Aimee's supplies were nearly gone. She certainly wanted that Silver Chest, but she still wondered what had happened and why there was an explosion.

Post-upgrade, Aimee no longer had to paddle. A control panel with buttons for up, down, left, and right allowed her to steer the raft as she pleased. Her speed had also increased by 2 knots.

She cautiously navigated around the floating loot and activated her Omniscient Eyes for a better view ahead. What she saw was mind-blowing.

[Whale Burst: When a Deepsea Whale reaches the end of its life, it triggers a Whale Burst, sacrificing itself to the ocean. After the explosion, random items drop, with quality based on the Whale Burst's level. (The Whale Burst ahead is Level 6, red.)]

Aimee pinched herself, not believing what she saw. 'Is this real? The Omniscient Eyes are incredibly powerful. What comprehensive knowledge!'

[The Ocean Core, the heart of the Deepsea Whale, is essential for Sea Beasts to evolve. When a Whale Burst occurs, all Sea Beasts go wild and swarm the whale's corpse.]

There was more information, but Aimee realized her Omniscient Eyes had run out. She quickly deactivated them and shut her eyes tight. Then a tear slipped down her cheek before she could stop it.

"I need to grab this loot before it disappears," Aimee muttered, downing an Energy Recovering Potion to restore her energy to full.

She grabbed her net and started tossing it in every direction. With so many chests floating, she didn't need her Omniscient Eyes. She threw the net, pulled it in, and put the loot in her System Bag.

There were Wooden Chests, Silver Chests, and extra Silver Chests. This was a true jackpot.

By the time her old fishing net's durability hit zero, she had pretty much collected every chest in the area.

Aimee activated her Omniscient Eyes again, scanning the spot where the Whale Burst had occurred. The red glow was gone, but now a blue light zipped around quickly, leaving orange and teal lights blinking out one after another.

She remembered what her Omniscient Eyes had revealed: [The Ocean Core, the heart of the Deepsea Whale, is essential for Sea Beasts to evolve. When a Whale Burst occurs, all Sea Beasts go wild and swarm the whale's corpse.]

'So, that blue light is definitely a Sea Beast,' she thought.

..............................................................................
Aimee swiftly twisted her elbow, reeled in her fishing rod still attached to a treasure chest, then powered up the oars and made her escape.

With the Deepsea Whale's carcass acting as bait nearby, she thought the predators wouldn't notice a small fry like her.

For almost an hour, the raft sped frantically across the water.

Aimee checked over her shoulder frequently, not stopping until the corpse and the blood-red sea vanished from sight.

For her own survival, Aimee pushed on for another ten minutes. Only when the ocean calmed down did she allow herself to relax.

'I'm wiped out. I can't take any more. Today was too exciting,' she thought. But glancing at the treasure chests in her System Bag, a grin spread across her face. 'No wonder they say, the bigger the storm, the bigger the catch.'

Aimee flopped back onto the raft, arms and legs stretched wide, laughing out loud. It was a wild experience, but the bounty made it worthwhile. Then she shot up, accessed her screen, and started sorting her loot.

[System Bag:]

[Blueprints: Antidote Potion Recipe (Basic) x1, Warm Clothing Blueprint x1, Wooden Gazebo Blueprint (Basic) x1]

[Weapons: Dagger (Crude) x1, Silvermoon Bow (Level 2) x1]

[Food: Strawberry Cream Bread x2, 7oz Sandwich Biscuits x1, Canned Beef Stew x1, 33.8 fl oz Mineral Water x1, 10 fl oz Mineral Water x2]

[Medicine: Fever Reducer (Box) x1, Hemostatic Potion x1, Energy Recovering Potion x1, Health Recovering Potion x2, Gauze x2]

But the real highlight was the stunning haul she had secured today. Her eyes sparkled with excitement, and her hands were itching to open her loot.

She had collected Wooden Chest x18, Bronze Chest x9, and Silver Chest x2. Before her escape, she also grabbed the Deepsea Whale's Beast Bone, perfect for upgrading her raft.

But the real treasure was the Gold Chest, her first one. A Silver Chest was equivalent to two or three Bronze ones, and a Gold Chest was in a league of its own.

Her hands shook with barely contained excitement as she held the treasure chests, but she forced herself to start with the Wooden Chests. She needed to replenish her food and supplies, as her raft upgrade had depleted her stock.

[Congratulations! You've received: Lumber x821, Iron Piece x477, Plastic x696, Stone x77, Resin x60, Frozen Chicken Drumstick x5, Solar Cooker x1, Fresh Cucumber x3, Charcoal x5, Pasta x1

[Level-1 Secret Key x2, Fork x3, Disposable Towel (Pack) x1, Freshly Cooked Pasta x3, Twine Rope x372, Yogurt Bread x10

[7oz Compressed Biscuits x1, 10 fl oz Mineral Water x13, 17 fl oz Sprite x1, 1.7oz Flamefish Meat x1, Gauze x6, 350 fl oz Whale Oil, 35oz Whale Meat.]

Not only had she recouped her upgrade costs, but she scored plenty of extras. The Wooden Chests mostly yielded basic supplies and food, enhancing her food diversity.

"Whoa, a cooker!" Aimee exclaimed, her eyes lighting up. Starving, she decided to boil some Frozen Chicken Drumsticks while sorting her items.

'The Level-1 Secret Key should unlock something cool, but I don't have whatever it opens yet,' she thought.

She hadn't even touched the Bronze or Silver Chests, and her supplies were already overflowing.

Upgrading her raft from Level-2 to Level-3 meant the material requirements had doubled again, and now there were unfamiliar items on the list.

[Lumber: 981/1,000, Iron Piece: 502/600, Plastic: 711/400, Iron Nail: 0/120, Resin: 95/100, Iron Anchor: 0/1, Furniture: 0/3, Level-3 Beast Bone: 0/1]

'Iron Nails and Iron Anchor? I swear I've seen those names somewhere,' Aimee thought, scanning her raft. 'But there's nothing except the workbench.' She got up and walked over, noticing a control panel on the far left.

[System Notification: Level-2 Raft upgrade successful. Workbench item crafting is now unlocked.]

'Whoa, a system notification? This thing is getting smarter,' Aimee thought as she approached the workbench. She hadn't fully examined it yet, too distracted by gathering supplies.

The workbench was sturdy, made from solid logs, with a smooth, splinter-free surface. On the left was a material input slot, and on the right, a light blue Crafting Interface was built into the table.

[Items you can craft at the workbench: Iron Nail: requires 3 Iron Pieces. Iron Pickaxe: requires 10 Lumber, 6 Iron Pieces.

[Iron Axe: requires 10 Lumber, 5 Iron Pieces. Fishing Rod: requires 15 Lumber, 3 Iron Pieces, and 2 Twine Ropes. Iron Anchor: requires 10 Iron Pieces.]

'As I thought,' Aimee thought, feeling pleased with herself as she used the workbench for the first time.

[Iron Piece consumed: 20/502. Crafting Iron Anchor x1.]

[Iron Anchor: It keeps your raft locked in place, preventing it from drifting.]

The sky turned dark suddenly. Aimee checked her wrist. It was 6:30 PM, still half an hour until nightfall. 'It shouldn't be getting dark this early,' she thought, puzzled.

However, with evening approaching, Aimee shrugged it off. She munched on her food while pulling up her holographic screen.

The Chat Channel was buzzing.

[Looking to trade blueprints! Anyone got any to swap?]

[Trading food for lumber. PM me if you're interested.]

[Why is it getting dark so fast? I've still got a bunch of chests to loot. What's up with the system?]

[Clocking out early? No complaints! This system is better than my boss.]

[We're here to survive, not work. The Novice Protection Period ends after today. After that, beasts won't be weakened anymore, and their spawn rate drops. Pressure is on.]

[Someone, help! I drank seawater, and now I've got a debuff: Dehydration. I'm desperate for water. Will trade a blueprint for mineral water.]

A guy lay sprawled on his tiny raft, barely able to speak. His hazy gaze rested on the stunning blue sky. It looked almost unreal.

He only meant to save some lumber and upgrade his raft, thinking a few sips of seawater wouldn't hurt. If only he'd known, but there was no taking it back.

Messages flooded the screen.

[Trading mineral water for a blueprint? Sure, I'll trade one 10 fl oz bottle.]

[That's stingy! A blueprint is worth more, right?]

[Easy for you to say. What are you offering? It's only the second day. Blueprints or water, what's more valuable? He's about to die, and I'm generous for trading.]

Snacktime: [LOL, one bottle of mineral water for a blueprint? I'll trade three bottles.]

Three bottles of 10 fl oz Mineral Water could stretch for three days. Most players couldn't afford that at this point.

[At least ask what blueprint it is. I know that. I wouldn't take it even if it were free.]

[You wouldn't take it for free? Is it that bad?]

'Blueprints?' Aimee thought, 'I don't have many.' She messaged the guy: [What kind of blueprint is it?]

He was negotiating with Snacktime and had only a Wooden Bed Blueprint, which was neither special nor particularly useful.

Realizing this, Snacktime was about to offer less.

The guy was still trying when he noticed the leaderboard big shot, the one who had been broadcast twice, approaching to trade. His eyes lit up.

Cash: [It's a Wooden Bed Blueprint. Your raft has enough space for it. I'm asking for three bottles of mineral water.]

Aimee's eyes sparkled. 'A Wooden Bed Blueprint? That's exactly what I need!'

Lucky: [Deal.]

After securing the blueprint, Aimee understood why no one wanted it.

[Wooden Bed Blueprint: A 5-foot double bed. Requires a raft area over 200 square feet to place. Materials needed: Lumber x100, Iron Nail x10, Resin x10, Fabric x3.]

It needed a lot of materials, and she'd need a workbench to create Iron Nails. Since looting more chests wasn't an option, she munched on a freshly cooked chicken drumstick and tossed the scraps into an empty wooden box.

"Might as well build the Wooden Gazebo and Wooden Bed first. Sleeping under the open sky feels too much like being lost in the wild," Aimee muttered, hair whipping in the sea breeze.

[Congratulations! Player Lucky has successfully built a Wooden Gazebo and a Wooden Bed.]

With a flash of light, two structures appeared. A 13x13-foot Wooden Gazebo, featuring four pillars and a classic roof, stood proudly on the raft, leaving ample space around it.

The Wooden Bed fit beneath the gazebo's roof so she wouldn't get wet even if it rained. Still open to the elements, it was vastly better than sleeping outside.

The bed was the true highlight, the one she had dreamed of for so long. She lay down, pulling her windbreaker over herself as a makeshift blanket. She settled in, finally feeling cozy and safe, and drifted off to sleep.

body.text:
The first thing Nicole did after waking up from the dead was return her boyfriend’s $1,700 birthday gift.

Then she spent every penny she had on food, medicine, weapons, and two steel security doors.

Everyone thought she had gone crazy.

Her boyfriend called her selfish. Her friends laughed at her.

But Nicole knew something they didn’t.

In exactly three days, the city would drown.

And this time, she refused to die for anyone.
——
"Ah!"
Nicole Floyd jolted upright in bed, gasping. Sweat streamed down her forehead, her eyes unfocused and hollow.
The sight in front of her cut through the haze in her mind.
This was her old apartment, the one from before the apocalypse.
Ding, ding…
Text alerts kept chiming. She grabbed her phone from the nightstand.
September 14, 2029. 9:32 a.m.
Nicole had more than a dozen unread messages. All of them were warning about a super typhoon named Cleaver, projected to make landfall early on the 17th along the coast. There would be category-breaking winds and days of relentless rain.
Nicole stared at the screen, dazed.
Hadn't she died? She remembered dying in that cannibal world devoid of light. Had her refusal to accept it dragged her into some dying hallucination?
Ding!
Another alert came in, updated at 9:37 a.m.
Nicole twisted her arm hard. Pain shot up her nerves, sharp and real.
This wasn't a dream. She had been reborn, back to three days before the storm that cracked the world open.
No. To be exact, two and a half days.
Nicole didn't feel happy. The exhaustion had settled deep in her bones. 
Typhoons, floods, deep freeze, extreme heat, earthquakes. One h311 after another. What was there worth reliving?
And yet, she was back.
Was she supposed to sit still and wait to die all over again?
Not a chance!
Nicole splashed cold water on her face. The mirror showed a younger version of herself with smooth skin and clear eyes, no hollowed-out desperation yet.
For a moment, everything looked fine.
Her gaze dropped to the crystal pendant at her neck.
She had been wearing it when she was abandoned at the hospital as a newborn. Later, Edward Austin had taken it from her and given it to the school's beauty queen, Mary Cannon.
Three years into the apocalypse, Mary still looked flawless. Her clothes were clean, her skin rosy, as if the old world never ended for her.
Once, when Nicole collapsed from hunger, she saw Mary casually pull a vanilla ice cream bar out of that pendant and lick it, slow and unbothered.
Nicole's breath hitched.
She grabbed a blade, sliced her fingertip, and let a drop of blood fall onto the pendant.
A blinding light exploded.
When her vision cleared, she stood inside an empty apartment with no front door. There was running water and electricity, but no furniture.
The place had two bedrooms and a living room, totaling about 860 square feet. The ceilings were nearly 10 feet high. Next to the balcony was a small garden, roughly 110 square feet, filled with dark soil.
A glowing timer floated in the living room.
01:56:13.
This was the storage space that let Mary live like royalty. Or rather, the one she had tricked out of Nicole's hands.
When Nicole stepped out, the space stayed with her, embedded in her mind. The moment she focused, she could sense everything inside.
Nicole tested it with boiling water. Everywhere except the balcony and the garden kept things perfectly fresh.
She could store things using thought alone. When nobody entered physically, the timer froze. Once she stepped inside, it started counting down.
There wasn't time to unravel how it worked.
She had a second life and a storage space. That was enough for her to change her gruesome fate last time.
In her past life, she had survived only three years. She had no idea what disasters came after.
With that in mind, Nicole searched online for types of natural disasters. When she looked at the results filling the screen, she nearly collapsed on the spot.
Gosh, staying alive was hard!
Pushing aside the extra emotions, she took out a pen and notebook and started listing supplies.
Nicole grew up in an orphanage. It looked peaceful on the surface, but underneath, the fighting was constant. That place taught her early how to protect herself and never take a loss.
She had been insecure by nature. In elementary school, she collected cardboard and recyclables. In middle school, she worked part-time tutoring, doing homework for others, and cleaning bathrooms. As long as it paid, she did it.
She ranked near the top in every major exam. Even after getting into the medical program and reaching her sophomore year, she was still tutoring five seniors preparing for college. She charged 40 d011ars per session.
Nicole had a nose for money. She had sold insurance and run a small video channel, chasing any legal hustle she could find. Over more than ten years, she had saved about 40 thousand d0llars, thinking that if she kept going, she'd have enough for a down payment by graduation.
Now, it was all meaningless.
She was supposed to have classes in the afternoon and tutoring at night, but none of that mattered anymore.
She messaged the parents, saying she had been hospitalized and wouldn't be able to tutor for a long time. She asked them to find replacements and settle the fees.
Tutoring fees were paid every two weeks. The parents weren't short on money. Two of them even sent her 100 d011ars as a get-well gift. Altogether, 1,200 d0llars hit her account.

Nicole pulled the curtain aside. Outside was a gray blur, wind and rain howling together. She thought it was still early, but her phone showed it was already after nine in the morning.
WhatsApp was exploding. The neighborhood group and class group both showed over 99 unread messages.
People were cheering the arrival of Typhoon Cleaver. Office workers were celebrating a break from endless overtime. Students were thrilled about the unexpected days off.
Photos and videos flooded the chats: trees ripped out by the roots, luxury cars crushed, a metal factory sliced open by a tornado.
Some people were starting to panic, complaining they hadn't stocked up on food. They said supermarkets were wiped clean by the time they got off work, with only a few sad packs of instant noodles left.
The drilling continued, coming from next door.
Nicole frowned. The building had three units per floor, and the other two were supposed to be empty.
In her last life, floodwater reached the second floor. People who fled their homes never got rescued and started targeting vacant apartments.
At first, everyone kept the peace. As food ran low, eyes grew darker, greed sharper. More than once, they tried to pry open Nicole's door in the middle of the night.
This time, she had a fire axe. If they tried, she wouldn't hesitate.
Then, she heard it. Not just drilling. A child's voice.
Nicole opened her door.
The door to unit 1801 was wide open. A brand-new stainless steel door leaned to the side. A young man in light-colored casual clothes was drilling into the wall.
Hearing her door open, he turned.
Nicole froze.
"It's you?"
